question.problem:
The joint probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.4$ | $0.3$ |

Find $\text{Var}[3X-Y].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y]+2ab\,\text{Cov}[X,Y].
$$

Also, the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2},
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.4$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.5$ | $0.5$ | $1$ |

Now, we can find $\text{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{X},$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.7 \\  & =1.4\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & ={0}^{2}\cdot 0.3+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.7 \\  & =2.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =2.8-{1.4}^{2} \\  & =0.84.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{Y},$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =0\cdot 0.5+1\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}{y}^{2}\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & ={0}^{2}\cdot 0.5+{1}^{2}\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =0.5-{0.5}^{2} \\  & =0.25.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's find $\text{Cov}[X,Y].$ We find $\text{E}[XY]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =0\cdot 0\cdot f(0,0)+0\cdot 1\cdot f(0,1)+2\cdot 0\cdot f(2,0)+2\cdot 1\cdot f(2,1) \\  & =0+0+0+2\cdot 0.3 \\  & =0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[XY] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =0.6-1.4\cdot 0.5 \\  & =-0.1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[3X-Y] & ={3}^{2}\cdot 0.84+(-1)^{2}\cdot 0.25+2\cdot 3\cdot (-1)\cdot (-0.1) \\  & =7.56+0.25+0.6 \\  & =8.41.\end{aligned}
$$
